files.purpose: ThreadRuntime.swift is the per-chat live engine: the @MainActor @Observable final class ThreadRuntime owns one thread's timeline entries and turn records, its provider session (warm-up, SessionSignature-driven relaunch, resume or start-over, epoch-guarded event handling through handle(_:)), the follow-up queue with drag bundling, revert and resend over git checkpoints with optional file restore, the diff caches and change stats, command-tree snapshots that recover shell edits, delta flush pacing (StreamLoad), persistence (scheduleSave, saveNow, snapshotForPersistence) and the whole Hydra lead/head machinery (streamed delegation-block parsing, HydraDelegationBudget, batches, the waiting queue, report turns, native heads, merge-state flags). The file also declares TimelineEntry, ReplyQuote (excerpt, peel), DraftCommand, ComposerDraft (outgoingText), PromptEdit, RuntimePhase, the private TimelineItem.Content.appendStreamed extension and the rehearsal extension used by website captures and native-head timelines. At B3 (1.7.0) it gains a recovery path for a CLI that is too old for the chosen model (finishTurnUpdatingCLI and resendAfterCLIUpdate run the CLI's own updater and send the failed message again, once per CLI version), two observable merge-queue flags, and a running-turn save interval that grows with the thread file's last written size. It also loses the uncalled hydraLiveInfo helper.

feature_notes: B3 adds a way to recover from a CLI that is too old for the model (SOURCE FACT, :2255-2293). finishTurnUpdatingCLI is consulted first on three failure paths: the startTurn catch (:1378, status .failed), .turnCompleted with an error (:2209, the event's own status) and .exited with an error while a turn runs (:2226, status .failed). It takes the error only when a turnID exists, the thread's provider passes ProviderRegistry.updatesOwnCLI (Claude or Codex only), and ProviderRegistry.needsNewerCLI matches. The match is case-insensitive and fires on any of 'or newer is required', 'requires a newer version', 'claude update', 'codex update', 'upgrade codex' or 'update codex'. When it takes the error, the raw error is NOT posted. An .info notice 'This model needs a newer <name>. Updating it, then sending your message again.' is appended inside the turn, and a Task awaits finishTurn(status:turnID:) and then resendAfterCLIUpdate. The caller neither posts the error nor ends the turn itself: it returns or breaks.

resendAfterCLIUpdate (:2272-2293): awaits app.providers.updateCLIIfDue(provider, force: true). It then reads installedCLIVersion. When that is nil, or equals cliResendVersions[provider] (the version this runtime already resent at), it appends the error notice '<error>

Droppy Code could not bring <name> up to date. Run `claude update`|`codex update` in Terminal, then send the message again.' and stops. Otherwise it records the version, releases the session with stop: true so the next send launches the new binary, and checks that the runtime is idle and that the turn still exists with a user item that is not from Hydra. If any check fails, it appends '<error>

<name> is up to date now (<version>). Send the message again.'. If they pass, it calls resend(turnID, text:, attachments:, restoreFiles: false), which reverts the failed turn (the info notice goes with it) and sends the same text and attachments. A throw appends '<name> is up to date now (<version>), but the message could not be sent again: <localizedDescription> Send it again.'. These three notices land after finishTurn has cleared currentTurnID and closingTurnID, so they are filed with no turn.

Consequence read from the source (not executed): the first attempt resends even if the updater did not change the version, because cliResendVersions starts empty. A second 'too old' failure at the same version then gets the 'could not bring up to date' notice. The limit is one resend per CLI version per runtime, and it is not persisted. On Codex, revert(to:) throws 'The selected message has no Codex turn ID, so its history cannot be safely reverted.' when the failed turn has no providerTurnID and the thread already has a providerSessionID (:1866-1868). That surfaces through the third notice.

Handler ordering changed. In .turnCompleted (:2206-2211) the turn id is captured before the error notice, then the CLI check runs, then 'if let error { appendNotice(.error, error) }', then finishTurn. In .exited (:2212-2229) the error notice now comes after the turn-id capture and the CLI check. The session is still released without stopping, approvals and questions are still cleared, and native heads are still stopped before the check. The fallback '<name> stopped unexpectedly.' for a nil error is unchanged.

Two new observed runtime flags (:313-317): isHydraMergeQueued ('This chat's finished work is waiting for another chat's merge to finish, and goes right after it') and hasHydraMergeRetryPending ('A quiet retry of a merge that failed in a way that clears by itself is scheduled'). This file only declares them. AppModel+HydraMerge.swift sets and reads them: :81 and :89-90 for the in-process merge queue, :415-420 for the 60-second retry. No B3 view reads them (git grep HEAD). holdsOnlyPersistedState (:3679-3686) does not include them.

scheduleSave while a turn runs (:3634-3647) no longer waits a fixed 5 s. The delay is seconds = min(20, max(5, bytes / 250_000)), with bytes = DiskWriter.shared.lastWrittenSize(of: Storage.threadURL(threadID)) ?? 0. That gives 5 s up to 1,250,000 bytes, then a linear rise to the 20 s cap at 5,000,000 bytes. The comment says 'five seconds up to a megabyte', which is approximate: the arithmetic keeps 5 s to 1.25 MB. The idle 800 ms debounce is unchanged. saveNow's comment still speaks of 'the five-second bound on what a crash costs' (:3654), which B3 made stale for large threads.

unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED: the Windows wording of the new failure notice 'Droppy Code could not bring <name> up to date. Run `claude update` in Terminal, then send the message again.'. OD-0012 F1 settles the product name ('Droppy Code' becomes 'Marrow'). OD-0012 G4 ('Terminal is Windows Terminal') is worded for the 'Open in' menu, and no ruling says whether 'in Terminal' in this notice follows it. The notice must be enumerated as a rename point (OD-0002) and the Terminal wording put to the owner.

UNRESOLVED: whether `claude update` and `codex update` behave the same way on Windows installs (npm, winget, native installer), and what installedCLIVersion's `--version` prints there. This is ProviderRegistry.swift's bundle, but this file's resend path depends on it.

UNRESOLVED: the ThreadRuntime.cs header still says it is ported from B2 :1-3758. Every source-line comment in the port must be re-cited to B3, or the owner must rule how B2 line comments are handled after the re-pin.
